key_insight: Multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated psychiatric intake improved a language model’s clinical interviewing performance and reduced acute-risk under-triage.
engineering_relevance: Validated simulation environments can support training and adversarial stress-testing of clinical conversational agents before supervised deployment.
method: Train a language model with multi-turn reinforcement learning in psychiatric intake simulations.
Compare it with an identically prompted base model in a randomized, double-blind crossover study.
Stress-test safety using 256 adversarial presentations derived from Delphi-consensus taxonomies.
evidence_signal: Across 60 matched scenario pairs (120 psychiatrist-enacted encounters), the trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of pairs; adversarial testing found acute-risk under-triage fell from 30.5% to 12.9%.
watch_item: Evaluation used simulated and psychiatrist-enacted patients, not real clinical care; residual safety gaps require safeguards and clinician oversight.
paper_title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
